nodes.title: Visual Language I
nodes.description: This course approaches drawing as both a technical skill and a method of inquiry. Through observation, structured experiments, and collaborative tasks, students will examine how drawing can be used to analyze and alter our understanding of objects, spaces, and concepts. The course focuses on drawing’s ability to construct, dismantle, and reconfigure visual forms. Students will use a range of materials, scales, and methods to explore ideas such as fragmentation, reconstruction, and conceptual development. By the end of the semester, each student will produce a set of works demonstrating a clear and reflective use of drawing as a flexible research tool.

nodes.title: Language of Drawing I
nodes.description: This introductory studio course presents drawing as a fundamental practice of observation, expression, and spatial thinking. Open to students from all disciplines, it explores drawing beyond technical skill, emphasizing its role as a tool for inquiry and communication across fields. Through diverse approaches and critical discussions, participants engage with mark-making, composition, and representation, developing a personal visual language applicable to their own practices.

nodes.title: Project and Internship
nodes.description: This is a non-credit, elective course that aims to foster field work experience in the student's chosen area of study. The course offers the students the opportunities to gain insights into the nuances of business and social environments; to learn about specific issues facing firms in the domestic and the global market; to improve their understanding of other cultures and societies; to foster research; to outreach to the global community. The course aims to enable students to learn about the conditions under which they would launch successful start-ups and expose them to the breadth of various issues. In order to realise these goals, the course includes experiential opportunities for students to put their new skills to work in real-world settings in line with their program requirements. A summer project or internship is mandatory for fulfilling the course requirements.
nodes.prereq_text: (PROJ 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D) or (PROJ 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D)

nodes.title: Art Studio I
nodes.description: Introduction to painting, sculpture and to basic notions of art making. Studio research into the numerous possibilities of various styles and approaches to visual art.
nodes.prereq_text: VA 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and VA 203 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Design Studio I
nodes.description: Coverage of the basic concepts of Graphic Design, such as Typography, Page Layout and Image creation and processing and their basic interactions.
nodes.prereq_text: VA 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and VA 203 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Art Studio III
nodes.description: After the intentionally eclectic program of the third studio year, the students at this stage are expected to move towards a personal approach to producing and reflecting about art. While the work becomes self-reliant, collective studio critiques will encourage and guide the student to ask the substantive questions about individual goals.
nodes.prereq_text: VA 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and VA 203 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Design Studio III
nodes.description: Introducing multimedia design elements; i.e. sound, interactivity, animation and the combination thereof within a graphic presentation.
nodes.prereq_text: VA 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and VA 203 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D
